newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Liberals have big lead before poll call.
newsitem.headline: Canada Liberals have big lead before poll call.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberals have a solid lead over their rivals in a federal election that will be called on Sunday and held June 2, according to a survey released on Friday.
The survey by Ekos Research Associates taken between March 18 and April 9 showed the Liberals backed by 41.7 percent of voters vs. 12.2 percent for the second-place Conservatives.
The right-wing Reform Party was supported by 10.6 percent of respondents, followed by the separatist Bloc Quebecois at 8 percent and the left-wing New Democrats at 6.5 percent.

The Ekos survey was based on interviews with 1,535 people from a panel of 3,000 randomly selected to participate in a project financed by some federal government departments, provincial governments and the private sector. The survey did not give a margin of error.
Chretien has laid the groundwork to announce his election call in Ottawa on Sunday for June 2 and fly to his hometown of Shawinigan, Quebec, for a rally that night.
"The election call will be Sunday," a government official said.
A second poll released on Friday showed the Bloc Quebecois with a clear lead over the Liberals in Quebec, although its lead narrowed from previous polls.

The Groupe Leger and Leger poll, commissioned by Toronto's Globe and Mail and Le Journal de Montreal, found that 43.1 percent of decided voters supported the Bloc versus 36.9 percent for the Liberals.
The previous Leger poll, taken in March, gave the Bloc a 45 percent to 32.2 percent lead over the Liberals.
The latest Leger poll, conducted from April 16 to April 22, surveyed 1,006 people with results considered accurate 19 times out of 20 and a margin of error of plus or minus 3.1 percentage points.

But the Globe said the poll showed a split among voters about whether a vote for the Bloc was the same as a vote for Quebec sovereignty. About four in 10 said the two were not the same, while six in 10 said it was equivalent to a vote for sovereignty.
The Bloc Quebecois is Canada's official opposition with 50 out of 295 seats in the House of Commons. It does not aim to form a government but to promote the Quebec separatist cause in Ottawa.
